unit.why: A single narrative about the Seer of Lublin and a young man whose death-decree is torn up by hasidim drinking 'lechaim' with him, followed by the author's moral and a closing encomium and death notice of the Seer.
unit.boundary_note: division ends with an appended encomium and the Seer's death date (Tisha B'Av 5575), not part of the narrative proper

stories.start_quote: הנה בהתגלות הצדיק הקדוש רבו החסידים
stories.end_quote: כזה קרעו גזר דינו ונוסף ימים על ימיו
stories.summary_en: A young man sneaks away from his family to spend Shavuot with the Seer of Lublin, who sends him straight home; at the inn, hasidim heading to Lublin drink 'lechaim' with him all night and bring him back, and the Seer explains that he had foreseen the man's death on the holiday, and that the hasidim's toasts, which accomplished what one tzaddik could not, tore up the decree.
